title: Sensors, Vol. 26, Pages 5928: Wearable Multi-Sensor Fusion for Field Assessment of Dynamic Postural Stability During the Curling Delivery in Young Adult Curlers: Integrating Trunk Kinematics, Plantar Pressure and Core-Muscle Activation
content: Postural control in curling is expressed during a dynamic, sport-specific delivery on a single sliding leg, yet it is still assessed almost exclusively with static single-leg force-plate protocols that poorly reflect on-ice demands. This study developed and validated a wearable multi-sensor system that fuses trunk and pelvis inertial measurement units (IMUs), instrumented plantar-pressure insoles and core-muscle surface electromyography (sEMG) to quantify dynamic postural stability during the simulated curling delivery in 110 young adult curlers (age range 18–24 years). A four-phase segmentation of the delivery was implemented, and a compact 28-feature set was extracted and combined through a complementary Kalman fusion scheme into a single Dynamic Stability Index (DSI). Validated against a reference force plate during static single-leg standing, the IMU-derived sway path showed a small bias (~0.4 cm) with 95% limits of agreement of approximately +4.4 to −3.6 cm, and between-day reliability of the fused DSI was excellent (ICC(3,1) = 0.90, 95% CI [0.82, 0.95]). A random-forest classifier discriminated high- from low-stability deliveries with 91.8% accuracy (95% CI [87.2%, 95.1%]; AUC = 0.92, 95% CI [0.87, 0.96]), outperforming any single-sensor or static force-plate baseline. Sensor-derived dynamic metrics correlated with external-oblique strength, trunk proprioceptive error and motor self-efficacy (Spearman ρ ranging from −0.55 to 0.51, all p < 0.001 after Holm–Bonferroni correction), and dynamic instability increased monotonically across descending self-efficacy tertiles. The proposed system provides a portable, context-relevant and interpretable tool for balance profiling in young curlers, and demonstrates that multi-sensor fusion substantially improves measurement fidelity over conventional single-modality assessment.

title: Há 200 anos, esta árvore foi plantada para salvar pessoas da fome. Hoje, ameaça florestas inteiras
content:
Araçá vermelho: Solução criada por pesquisadores une tecnologia e natureza para combater uma espécie invasora presente no Havaí há 200 anos (Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil)
Repórter
Publicado em 20 de setembro de 2026 às 16h27.
Em 1825, autoridades do Havaí introduziram uma espécie brasileira com o objetivo de ampliar as fontes de alimento da população local. O araçá vermelho, conhecido cientificamente como Psidium cattleianum, encontrou no arquipélago condições favoráveis para se desenvolver e, com o passar das décadas, tornou-se uma espécie invasora, organismo levado para um ambiente diferente de sua origem e capaz de causar alterações no ecossistema.
A planta brasileira, inicialmente considerada uma alternativa alimentar, passou a ocupar grandes áreas do território havaiano e formar florestas densas que dificultam o crescimento da vegetação nativa.Sem os mecanismos naturais de controle existentes em seu habitat original, o araçá vermelho se espalhou pelo ambiente havaiano. A ausência de predadores e competidores naturais permitiu que a árvore ocupasse áreas extensas, modificando a composição das florestas locais.
O avanço da espécie criou um desafio para pesquisadores e órgãos ambientais, que passaram a buscar formas de reduzir sua presença sem causar impactos sobre outras plantas e animais. A solução encontrada envolve um inseto brasileiro e o uso de drones, veículos aéreos não tripulados usados para aplicações em áreas remotas.
Para combater a expansão do araçá vermelho, pesquisadores utilizaram o Tectococcus ovatus, inseto originário do Brasil que possui uma relação específica com a planta. O organismo se alimenta exclusivamente do araçá vermelho, característica que permite um controle mais direcionado da espécie.
Em 2012, autoridades havaianas aprovaram o uso do inseto como agente de controle biológico, método que utiliza organismos vivos para reduzir populações de espécies consideradas prejudiciais. O Tectococcus ovatus cria pequenas estruturas chamadas galhas nas folhas da árvore, que afetam seu desenvolvimento.
O controle biológico com o inseto brasileiro foi adotado como uma estratégia para reduzir o crescimento do araçá vermelho sem atingir outras espécies presentes no ecossistema havaiano.A aplicação do inseto representa uma alternativa aos métodos químicos, pois atua diretamente sobre a espécie-alvo. O objetivo dos pesquisadores é limitar a expansão da árvore invasora e preservar áreas de vegetação nativa.
A etapa mais recente do projeto envolve a utilização de drones para ampliar a distribuição do inseto controlador. Um estudo publicado no Journal of Economic Entomology avaliou a diferença entre a aplicação manual e o uso de aeronaves automatizadas.
Os resultados indicaram redução no tempo necessário para tratar cada árvore. O método tradicional levava aproximadamente 12 minutos por planta, enquanto o sistema com drones reduziu esse período para 2,8 minutos.
A aplicação por drones reduziu em 77% o tempo de operação e aumentou a taxa de colonização do inseto nas árvores tratadas de 38% para 63% após um ano.A tecnologia também permite alcançar regiões de mata com acesso limitado, ampliando a área de atuação do programa e reduzindo as dificuldades logísticas enfrentadas pelas equipes de campo.
Após os primeiros resultados, pesquisadores desenvolveram uma estrutura com maior capacidade de distribuição de insetos. A iniciativa recebeu o nome de Kūhualūlū e tem como foco acelerar o controle do araçá vermelho em áreas de difícil acesso.
O projeto combina automação e controle biológico para proteger ecossistemas nativos do Havaí afetados pela expansão da espécie introduzida há cerca de dois séculos.
Pesquisadores avaliam que a combinação entre agentes biológicos específicos e drones pode ser aplicada em outros programas de manejo de espécies invasoras em diferentes regiões do mundo.A iniciativa segue em desenvolvimento para ampliar a escala de aplicação e avaliar os efeitos de longo prazo sobre as áreas afetadas pela presença do araçá vermelho.

title: Agentic Detection of Online Conspiracies
content: Conspiratorial discourse on social media is not always expressed through explicit claims or stable lexical markers. The same surface content may express endorsement, legitimate concerns, criticism, satire, or mockery. The main challenge is therefore not only recognizing conspiracy-related claims, but inferring the speaker's intent -- the utterance's illocutionary force. We argue that this can be achieved through the use of relevant social contexts and propose an agentic framework, equipped with a set of tools supporting social queries. We demonstrate the benefits of our approach on a unique dataset of Hebrew tweets, covering 80\%--90\% of the public Hebrew tweets published over a four-year span (late 2018-- early 2023), encompassing several election cycles as well as the COVID pandemic years and related vaccination campaigns. This extensive coverage can be used in recovering different social contexts. Evaluating our framework on a manually-annotated adversarial dataset, we find that context-aware workflows consistently outperform text-only classification and that the agentic framework performs significantly better than other frameworks and settings, including a non-agentic model exposed to the same contexts available to the agent. We further provide an analysis of the results, the errors and efficiency (token economy) tradeoffs. These findings support viewing the task of conspiracy detection as a socially embedded interpretation task, in which effective classification depends not only on access to contexts, but also on adaptive reasoning in which the agent uses tools on a per-case basis, asking only for evidence relevant to its current reasoning step.

title: Monet time: French Renaissance painter's rarely seen 'Iris' set to break sale record
content:
A total of 28 works from the Schlumberger collection are being sold at Sotheby's France. Valued at more than €40 million, they include four paintings by Claude Monet, pieces by Paul Cézanne and Gustave Moreau, and a sculpture by Camille Claudel.
Between €22 and 30 million, the highest estimate ever placed on a painting sold in France. That is what a buyer could spend to obtain 'Iris' by Claude Monet.
On 22 October, Sotheby's auction house will be offering the rarely seen work by the French Renaissance master for sale, alongside other works from the Schlumberger family's private collection.
A monumental painting created by Monet at the end of his life, the canvas is, according to curators, in remarkable condition. _"_It has no varnish, it is on its original canvas and has never been restored. They are exactly as Monet painted them 100 years ago," explains Thomas Bompard, co-director of the Modern and Contemporary Department at Sotheby's France.
Canvases preserved in the Schlumberger living room
Every detail counts. Varnish alters the chromatic tones of a painting, according to art historian Marianne Mathieu.
But restoration could damage the texture of the paint on the canvas. "Late Monet is a Monet who works the material. So to truly discover and understand him, that material has to be preserved. And we still have these thick impastos."
Hung in a Schlumberger family sitting room for a century, 'Iris', like 'Weeping Willow', also up for sale and valued at between nine and ten million euros, has never been moved.
Above all, it has never been seen in colour by the general public. It was acquired by Jeanne Schlumberger (1889-1983), "a brilliant art collector", from the painter's family through "the visionary gallerist" Katia Granoff, according to Thomas Bompard, without going through an auction room.
"Many people knew the story, or at least knew of the existence of this collection; people whispered that these were the finest Monets in Paris, but very few had actually seen them. That is also what is fuelling today's excitement," he notes.
A collection valued at €40 million
Another factor that has pushed prices higher is the centenary of the death of the Impressionist artist, who died on 5 December 1926. Two exhibitions on the painter's life open in Paris at the end of September: "Monet, Painting Time" and "Stories of Landscapes, from Monet to Hockney".
In all, 28 works are up for auction at Sotheby's, in a sale expected to raise more than €40 million. Among them are four Monets, as well as a sculpture by Camille Claudel and several paintings by Gustave Moreau.
Also being sold on this occasion is a wall composition of three works by Paul Cézanne. "La Ferme", the central painting, is "the largest work by the artist ever to be offered at auction" and is estimated at between €600,000 and €800,000.
The three paintings have been designated as "national treasures", a measure intended to give the state 30 months in which to arrange a possible acquisition.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Nomogram for Delayed Treatment in Pediatric Testicular Torsion: A Retrospective Study Spanning Over Two Decades.
content: Testicular torsion (TT) is a time-sensitive pediatric urologic emergency in which delayed treatment markedly reduces the likelihood of testicular salvage. This study aimed to identify factors associated with delayed treatment in children with TT and to develop and internally validate a nomogram for retrospective characterization of delay-risk profiles. A total of 540 pediatric patients with surgically confirmed TT were retrospectively included and randomly assigned to a training cohort (n=377) and a validation cohort (n=163). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression was used for variable selection in the training cohort, followed by multivariable logistic regression to construct the final model and nomogram. Model performance was evaluated by discrimination, calibration, decision curve analysis (DCA), and bootstrap internal validation. Nine predictors were retained for final model development: age, sports or injuries, persistent symptoms, onset during sleep, misdiagnosis, degree of cord twisting > 180°, guardian awareness of TT, transfer distance, and ipsilateral hydrocele. The nomogram showed good discrimination, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.952 (95% CI, 0.932-0.973) in the training cohort and 0.940 (95% CI, 0.904-0.976) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed probabilities. DCA indicated potential net benefit in both cohorts. To our knowledge, this study developed the first nomogram for retrospectively characterizing delay-risk profiles in children with TT. Internal validation showed good retrospective discrimination within the study cohorts. This nomogram may help identify clinical and care-pathway patterns relevant to quality improvement.

title: Pilule contraceptive: faut-il s'inquiéter après l'alerte sur le désogestrel ?
content:
Encore très prescrite en France, la pilule contraceptive a mauvaise presse auprès d'un nombre croissant de femmes, en raison de ses effets secondaires. L'Agence du médicament (ANSM) a décidé d'informer 1,6 million de femmes prenant du désogestrel, d'un faible risque de méningiome, une tumeur au cerveau le plus souvent non cancéreuse.
La pilule reste-t-elle un choix sûr?
Que signifie l'alerte de l'ANSM ?
Les pilules à base du progestatif désogestrel (Antigone, Cerazette, Elfasette, Optimizette...) représentent près de la moitié des pilules contraceptives utilisées en France. Les pilules combinant un oestrogène et un progestatif associant lévonorgestrel et éthinylestradiol représentent l'autre moitié.
Elles sont en général "prescrites chez les femmes qui ont plus de problèmes cardiovasculaires", car elles ne sont "pas associées à un risque de thrombose", et sont "plébiscitées par les femmes en post-partum et pendant l'allaitement", souligne le Dr Isabelle Yoldjian, directrice médicale de l'ANSM.
Une étude phare a confirmé un sur-risque "faible" de méningiome (1 cas pour 67.000 utilisatrices, 1 pour 17.000 après cinq ans de prise) chez les femmes prenant du désogestrel de façon prolongée, en particulier après 45 ans, et chez celles ayant pris auparavant un progestatif à risque (Androcur, Lutényl, Lutéran).
L'agence du médicament écrit ainsi à quelque 1,6 million de femmes ayant pris du désogestrel pour les informer de ce risque.
"En aucun cas, cette contraception n'est remise en question", souligne le Dr Yoldjian.
Doit-on craindre les pilules ?
Non, répondent les professionnels de santé. Les effets secondaires les plus fréquemment rapportés sont des saignements irréguliers, prise de poids, troubles de l'humeur, baisse de libido... Mais "la balance bénéfices/risques reste toujours extrêmement favorable", veut rassurer le Dr Geoffroy Robin, gynécologue au CHU de Lille.
Car au-delà d'éviter des grossesses non désirées, certaines pilules ont aussi des bénéfices secondaires: elles soulagent les douleurs liées à l'endométriose et protègent de certains cancers: côlon, endomètre, ovaire.
Pour Isabelle Derrendinger, présidente du Conseil national de l'Ordre des sages-femmes, cette alerte illustre surtout "la déficience en données scientifiques sur la santé des femmes", qu'on est en train de rattraper.
Une désaffection croissante ?
En 2005, plus de la moitié des femmes de 18 à 49 ans recouraient à la pilule contraceptive. En 2023, elles n'étaient plus que 26,8%, selon l'enquête "Contexte des sexualités en France" (Inserm, 2024).
Chez les plus jeunes (18-29 ans), elle reste la méthode la plus utilisée mais a chuté à 36,6% en 2023 contre 54,3% en 2016, en particulier depuis la révélation, en 2013, de risques accrus liés aux pilules de 3e et 4e générations. Cette année-là, une jeune femme restée handicapée après un AVC avait porté plainte contre le fabricant d'une pilule de 3e génération - un dossier classé sans suite en 2017.
Depuis, règne "un climat d'hormonophobie", regrette le Dr Robin, alimenté notamment par "beaucoup de désinformation sur les réseaux sociaux".
Nombre de jeunes femmes souhaitent retrouver un cycle "plus naturel" et certaines optent pour des pratiques alternatives: méthode du calendrier, observation de la température corporelle, de la glaire cervicale.
Mais leur efficacité est "modeste" et elles ne conviennent pas aux femmes aux cycles irréguliers, rappelle le Dr Robin.
Quelles sont les méthodes les plus plébiscitées ?
Le stérilet arrive en tête des méthodes de contraception utilisées chez les femmes de 18 à 49 ans avec 27,7% d'utilisatrices (Inserm) en 2023: aujourd'hui mieux formés, les gynécologues le proposent désormais aussi aux femmes sans enfant.
La contraception repose encore principalement sur les femmes même si le nombre de vasectomies (stérilisation masculine définitive) a été multiplié par 26 en quinze ans, pour atteindre 57.666 en 2025 (étude Epi-Phare).
Plébiscité par plus d'une femme de 18 à 29 ans sur quatre (22,3% en 2023) le préservatif pourrait être encore utilisé davantage, estime Mme Derrendinger, pour qui "il faut beaucoup plus craindre les infections sexuellement transmissibles que le risque de méningiome avec le désogestrel".
Lire aussiMédicaments à base de désogestrel : une surveillance limitée face à des risques jugés faibles
Pourquoi faut-il réévaluer sa contraception régulièrement ?
Il n'existe pas de méthode de contraception idéale: celle qui convient à 20 ans n’est pas la même qu'à 40 ans: le corps, la santé, les projets de vie évoluent. Elle doit donc être réévaluée régulièrement avec un médecin, une sage-femme ou un gynécologue, au vu de ses éventuels effets secondaires et ses bénéfices. L'ANSM conseille, à partir de 35 ans, de faire un bilan hormonal des traitements pris jusque-là.

title: Kronkorken sammeln: Deshalb solltest du sie nicht in den Restmüll werfen
content:
Besser als sie wegzuwerfen ist es, Kronkorken zu sammeln. Die kleinen Deckel lassen sich nämlich gut recyceln. Die Erlöse daraus kommen teilweise sogar sozialen Projekten zugute.
Nach einer Party oder einem Grillabend sammeln sich schnell Kronkorken an – und manchmal landen sie in der Umwelt. Dass das nicht gut ist, sollte selbstverständlich sein. Der Kunststoffanteil (PET) der Kronkorken zersetzt sich mit der Zeit zu Mikroplastik. In den Restmüll gehören die Kronkorken aber ebenso wenig, da sich sowohl der Kunststoff- als auch der Weißblechanteil gut recyceln lassen.
So entsorgst du Kronkorken richtig:
- Einzelne Kronkorken kannst du in die gelbe Tonne werfen.
- Große Mengen kannst du zu einem Wertstoffhof bringen oder bei Wertstoffinseln in den Container für Dosen/Alu werfen.
Kronkorken sammeln und Gutes bewirken
Noch besser ist es, wenn du die Kronkorken nicht direkt zum Wertstoffhof bringst, sondern bei der Sammelstelle einer gemeinnützigen Organisation abgibst. Deren Mitglieder bringen die Kronkorken dann zum Wertstoffhof und finanzieren von dem Erlös gemeinnützige Projekte.
Online findest du verschiedene solcher Angebote:
- Die Aktion Kronkorken ohne Grenzen unterstützt verschiedene Hilfsprojekte des Vereins Rotary-Hilfe-Tholey-Bostalsee e.V. Sammelstellen gibt es etwa in der Gegend rund um Freisen zwischen Trier und Kaiserslautern.
- Eco Projects Global sammelt Kronkorken, aber auch Deckel aus Plastik und Aluminium, und gibt sie sortenrein ins Recycling. Aus dem Erlös werden unter anderem Nachhaltigkeitsprojekte unterstützt. Zugehörige Abgabestellen gibt es zum Beispiel in Hamburg, Berlin und Nürnberg.
Kronkorken sammeln und tauschen
Manche Kronkorken mit hübschen Designs sind eigentlich zu schade zum Wegwerfen. Ohnehin lohnt es sich, verschiedene Kronkorken zu sammeln: Du kannst sie etwa mit anderen Sammler:innen tauschen und sie als Urlaubs-Souvenir mitnehmen.
Weltweit und vor allem in Deutschland gibt es eine riesige Menge verschiedener Kronkorken und ständig entstehen neue. Zudem nehmen die Deckel wenig Platz weg und kosten gar nichts bis wenig. Auch Kinder können großen Spaß daran haben, draußen interessante Kronkorken zu sammeln.
Kronkorken sammeln: Kreative Ideen
Was kannst du mit gesammelten Kronkorken anstellen? Für die kleinen Deckel gibt es mehr Verwendungsmöglichkeiten, als es zunächst scheint. Hier sind ein paar Upcycling-Ideen:
- Kronkorken eignen sich hervorragend zum Basteln von Rasseln. Bohre dafür Löcher in die Mitte der Kronkorken, fädele sie auf ein Stück stabilen Draht und spanne den Draht in eine Astgabel ein.
- Besonders hübsche Kronkorken machen sich gut als Anhänger für Ohrringe. Dafür musst du nur ein kleines Loch in den Rand bohren und einen Ohrhänger einfädeln. Oder du machst dir zunutze, dass die kleinen Deckel von Magneten angezogen werden: Befestige am Ohrhänger einen gebogenen Magneten und verbinde ihn mit einem der Kronkorken. Dieses Design ist zwar etwas aufwendiger, du kannst aber dafür die Kronkorken nach Belieben austauschen.
- Lege Mosaike aus Kronkorken und verziere damit zum Beispiel eine flache Obstschale aus Bambus. Klebe dafür einfach Kronkorken mosaikartig auf die Schüssel und fülle die Zwischenräume mit Fugenmasse auf.

title: Deutschland tritt UN-Hochseeschutzabkommen bei
content:
Gegen Müll und Überfischung Deutschland tritt UN-Hochseeschutzabkommen bei
Plastikmüll, Überfischung und Klimawandel belasten die Ozeane. Zum Schutz der Hochsee gibt es deshalb ein UN-Abkommen - und Deutschland ist dem nun beigetreten. Es geht um den Schutz von zwei Dritteln der Meeresfläche.
Seit Anfang des Jahres ist das Hochseeschutzabkommen der Vereinten Nationen in Kraft. Es ist die rechtliche Grundlage für den Schutz der internationalen Gewässer auf hoher See. Jetzt ist auch Deutschland dem UN-Abkommen offiziell beigetreten. Bundesumweltminister Carsten Schneider hinterlegte die entsprechende Ratifizierungsurkunde bei den Vereinten Nationen.
Der SPD-Politiker würdigte das Abkommen als den größten internationalen umweltpolitischen Erfolg der vergangenen Jahre. "Das Abkommen beweist, dass auch in konfrontativen Zeiten das Prinzip der Zusammenarbeit international immer noch auf große Zustimmung stößt", teilte Schneider am Rande der UN-Vollversammlung in New York mit.
Ein Abkommen für etwa zwei Drittel der Meeresfläche
Das UN-Hochseeschutzabkommen trägt den offiziellen Namen "Agreement on Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction" (BBNJ-Agreement). Es gilt für die Regionen der Meere, die außerhalb der nationalen Hoheitsgewässer bis zwölf Seemeilen und außerhalb der nationalen Wirtschaftszone bis 200 Seemeilen liegen. Das umfasst zwei Drittel der Meeresfläche.
Nur gesunde Meere könnten Menschen mit Sauerstoff und Nahrung versorgen, erklärte Schneider. Momentan sei deren Zustand aber schlecht: Plastikmüll, Überfischung, Chemikalien und Klimawandel belasteten die Meere weltweit. Umso wichtiger sei es, Rückzugsräume zu schaffen, in denen sich die Natur wieder erholen könne. Die Erfahrung zeige, dass diese zurückkehre, wenn Meeresflächen zu Schutzgebieten würden.
Erste Ozean-COP im Januar
Das UN-Abkommen sowie das für dessen Umsetzung auf nationaler Ebene bereits im Frühjahr vom Bundestag verabschiedete notwendige Hochseeschutzgesetz werden nach Angaben des Umweltministeriums 30 Tage nach dem Beitritt, also am 21. Oktober, für deutsche Akteure verbindlich. Das heißt, dass sich deutsche Organisationen und Personen, darunter etwa Schiffe unter deutscher Flagge oder deutsche Hochseeforscherinnen und -forscher, dann an die Regeln des Abkommens halten müssen.
Dazu zählen neben dem Einrichten von Meeresschutzgebieten unter anderem auch verbindliche Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfungen von menschlichen Aktivitäten in den Gewässern. Außerdem ist der Umgang mit Proben mariner Tiere und Pflanzen in dem Abkommen geregelt. Ärmere Länder des globalen Südens sollen zudem bei Schutz und nachhaltiger Nutzung der Biodiversität unterstützt werden.
Die erste Vertragsstaatenkonferenz des Hochseeschutzabkommens der Vereinten Nationen, die sogenannte Ozean-COP, soll dann im Januar 2027 in New York stattfinden. Die Ausweisung von Meeresschutzgebieten wird nach Angaben des Umweltministeriums voraussichtlich erst bei späteren Konferenzen beginnen.

title: Tirzepatide versus other anti-diabetic agents for the prevention of diabetic foot complications in patients with type 2 diabetes
content: BackgroundDiabetic foot complications affect up to 25% of patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and represent a major cause of morbidity. The dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist - tirzepatide (TZP) has demonstrated superior glycemic control compared with semaglutide however, evidence regarding its effects on diabetic foot complications (DFCs) remains limited.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX network. Adults with T2D initiating TZP, sulfonylurea (SU), dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4is), sodium–glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2is), and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) between January 2022 and July 2025 were included. Propensity score matching created balanced cohorts for four comparisons. The primary outcome was the risk of DFC - a composite of ulcers, infections, critical limb ischemia, and revascularization or amputation.ResultsAfter matching, four cohorts included 141,002 patients per arm (TZP vs. SU), 131,449 patients per arm (TZP vs. DPP-4i), 146,321 patients per arm (TZP vs. SGLT2i), and 97,457 patients per arm (TZP vs. GLP-1RA). Compared with SU, TZP was associated with reduced diabetic foot complications (HR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.76–0.84). Similar reductions were observed versus DPP-4i (HR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.78–0.87) and SGLT2i (HR, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.83–0.92). No difference was found versus GLP-1RA (HR, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.91–1.03).ConclusionTZP was associated with a reduction in diabetic foot complications compared with SU, DPP-4i, and SGLT2i, with outcomes similar to GLP-1RA. These findings suggest tirzepatide may be a valuable option for patients at risk of ulceration or amputation.

title: Youth-Led Forest Restoration Movement Traces Back to a 9-Year-Old’s Question About Climate Change
content:
A boy who learned about Wangari Maathai’s tree-planting legacy at age nine sparked a youth-led forest restoration movement now training over 100,000 young Climate Justice Ambassadors across 76 countries.
Youth-led forest restoration at Plant-for-the-Planet began in 2007, when nine-year-old Felix Finkbeiner in Germany learned about Kenyan Nobel laureate Wangari Maathai’s campaign planting 30 million trees across Africa. Struck by her message that trees serve as powerful allies against global warming, Finkbeiner proposed that every country commit to planting one million trees. By age 13, he stood before the United Nations General Assembly, raising that ambition to one trillion trees worldwide.
Nearly two decades later, youth-led forest restoration has grown from one child’s conviction into a global movement operating academies across 76 countries. More than 104,800 children and youth have become Climate Justice Ambassadors, trained to understand the climate crisis and empowered to fight for their future through tree planting, public speaking, and community organizing. The organization has facilitated more than 36 million trees planted directly through its own restoration projects, while its platform has funded over 107 million trees through partner organizations worldwide.
The model driving youth-led forest restoration rests on a simple premise: young people affected most by climate change deserve genuine agency in addressing it, not token participation. At Plant-for-the-Planet Academies, Ambassadors learn climate science, then apply that knowledge locally, giving speeches, organizing tree-planting events, and mobilizing their communities. This youth leadership extends into formal governance through the Global Ambassadors Council, the organization’s official youth leadership body shaping strategic direction.
Restoration work spans three countries, each addressing distinct ecological challenges. In Mexico’s Yucatán Peninsula, youth-led forest restoration protects and regrows Mayan rainforest, with more than 17.8 million trees planted, two reserves under active patrol, and work underway establishing a jaguar wildlife corridor connecting fragmented habitat. In Ghana, community-based restoration addresses degradation across the Savannah Ecological Zone, tackling climate vulnerability and poverty simultaneously through Plant-for-Ghana. In Spain, restoration projects are reviving lost forest landscapes around Granada, Doñana, Madrid, and Barcelona.
Beyond planting trees directly, youth-led forest restoration extends its impact through free technology supporting restoration organizations worldwide. Forest Cloud provides funding, management, and monitoring tools for restoration projects at no cost to nonprofits and communities, and has already enabled more than 100 million trees to be funded through the platform. FireAlert monitors 1.6 billion hectares for wildfire risk, allowing rapid response before fires spread. TreeMapper helps organizations track restoration progress with scientific rigor, while SeedManager, still in development, will support biodiverse ecosystem restoration specifically.
This technology-sharing approach reflects a deliberate strategic shift. Rather than measuring success purely by trees planted, satellite imagery and hectare-based tracking now anchor the organization’s accountability, providing longer-term verification of genuine forest recovery rather than short-term planting counts alone. Free restoration advice and published research further extend support to restoration organizations beyond Plant-for-the-Planet’s own direct projects.
Youth-led forest restoration also encompasses direct policy advocacy. The organization pushes for policies enabling forest conservation and climate justice, including transparency initiatives like TFFF Watch, which monitors accountability within international rainforest funding mechanisms, and Tracer, a tool supporting deforestation-free supply chains under European Union regulations.
National entities extend this youth-led forest restoration model across eight countries with independent operations. Ghana’s affiliate has empowered 2,400 Climate Justice Ambassadors while planting over 227,000 trees. Spain’s chapter, active since 2013, has trained over 5,100 Ambassadors through 151 academies while planting more than 501,000 trees. Since 2015, Czechia has mobilized youth and national celebrities alike, engaging over 1,000 Ambassadors. Each national entity adapts the core model, youth empowerment paired with forest restoration, to its own climate and community context.
Corporate partnerships increasingly fund this expansion. Companies can grow dedicated forest plots, support deforestation-free supply chains, and educate their workforce on climate action through structured partnership programs. Change Chocolate, a fair-trade product line, generates revenue that directly supports community forest protection in tropical regions vulnerable to deforestation pressure.
What distinguishes youth-led forest restoration from conventional reforestation charities is this persistent emphasis on intergenerational leadership. Ambassadors don’t simply volunteer for adult-designed programs; they shape strategy through elected councils, speak at international forums, and carry restoration knowledge into their own communities as they grow into adulthood. Finkbeiner himself, once a nine-year-old inspired by a Nobel laureate’s tree-planting campaign, now leads an organization where the next generation of nine-year-olds continues that same cycle of learning and action.
Nearly twenty years after one child’s question about climate change reached a global stage, youth-led forest restoration demonstrates that meaningful climate action doesn’t require waiting for adulthood or institutional permission. It requires forests, young people willing to fight for them, and the tools to turn that determination into hectares of restored, thriving ecosystems.

title: Lewis Hamilton’s £20m Mission 44 opens opportunities for young people
content:
Lewis Hamilton, the seven time Formula One World Champion, might be a multi millionaire but he has always been committed to giving back to society. The F1 legend Lewis Hamilton has kept his focus on his career but it seems his mission has marked another remarkable milestone.
Lewis Hamilton’s foundation reached a record breaking number of students across continents after he pledged £20 million to it
In 2021, Lewis Hamilton had pledged a whopping £20 million to a new charity he founded, Mission 44, which was focused on bringing new opportunities to youth from under represented groups in the United Kingdom.
Now, Mission 44 has marked a new milestone as it has reached over 550,000+ young people globally across the UK, US, and Brazil.
In a previous interview with ESPN, Lewis Hamilton reflected on pledging £20 million to his charity as he said, "Supporting the ambitions of underrepresented young people has always been important to me and Mission 44 represents my commitment to create real change within this community…”
The F1 legend added, “In my early life, I experienced first-hand how coming from an underrepresented background can affect your future but, luckily for me, I was able to overcome those odds through opportunity and support. I want to ensure that other young people from similar backgrounds are able to do the same.
Lewis Hamilton continued, "I am so grateful that Mercedes are joining me on our initiative Ignite, with the goal to improve representation within the motorsport industry. The findings of The Hamilton Commission and its recommendations have provided us with a fantastic basis to begin our work. Change within the industry is long overdue, but we are now firmly on the journey towards transforming it for the better."
Lewis Hamilton has constantly worked on providing more educational and work opportunities to youth
For the unversed, the F1 legend Lewis Hamilton was wrongly removed from his school when he was 15 years old. Today, his foundation,Mission 44, works on rising suspension and exclusion rates by funding tailored mentorship and providing school support networks to students across continents.
But that’s not all; the data from the Hamilton Commission revealed that less than 1% of F1 engineering roles were held by Black professionals. Lewis Hamilton’s foundation, Mission 44, has worked on awarding motorsport scholarships and brings students directly onto F1 tracks to break into tech and engineering fields.
Apart from that, the F1 legend Lewis Hamilton has also met officials at 10 Downing Street to actively push for systemic national framework changes in classroom inclusivity.
While the Mission 44 was founded majorly to help Black youths, it has since extended its services to all under represented groups across continents in UK, US, and Brazil.

title: Agency says sea turtle eggs laid on California beaches are a first for the US West Coast
content:
HUNTINGTON BEACH, Calif. (AP) — A reptile believed to be struggling in sand at a Southern California beach was simply making history: a sea turtle laying eggs on the U.S. West Coast.
And three days later, there were more. An olive ridley turtle — maybe the same one — laid eggs on Sept. 19, a few miles away near the Huntington Beach Pier in Orange County, authorities said.
“This is the first-ever recorded natural nesting for any sea turtle species” on the West Coast, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s West Coast Fisheries division said on Facebook.
Olive ridley turtles are the smallest of sea turtles, with adults weighing up to 100 pounds (45.3 kilograms). NOAA said they’re found worldwide but primarily in the tropical waters of the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans.
The first nesting spot was near Seal Beach on Sept. 16, followed by the discovery at Huntington Beach. Both sites were subsequently fenced off. Incubation typically lasts 45 to 60 days, NOAA said.
“We’re excited about it,” said Trevor McDonald, marine safety chief at the Huntington Beach Fire Department.
Lifeguards patrolling at night saw a turtle digging in the sand and thought “maybe this turtle is sick. We just don’t see this very often,” McDonald said. “Then they observed the turtle starting to lay eggs.”
Heidi Stephen said her 9-year-old son, Jude, begged her to take him to Huntington Beach to see the nest Tuesday.
“It’s so magical,” Stephen said.
George Zamora said he hopes the eggs can survive any impact from tides, storms and popular beach events.
“Let them do their thing,” Zamora said. “Let them be born.”
By Eugene Garcia and Ed White, Associated Press

title: Fundo Vale usa R$ 1 como isca e mobiliza R$ 5,9 para a floresta
content:

Nova York - Para cada R$ 1 que aportou, o Fundo Vale diz ter mobilizado outros R$ 5,9 de bancos, fundos, organismos internacionais e investidores públicos.
Este é o dado central do Relatório de Impacto da Vale ao qual a EXAME teve acesso em primeira mão, a ser divulgado nas próximas semanas, e parece traduzir uma aposta: usar o capital do fundo não como financiamento permanente, mas como capital catalítico, capaz de atrair capital de terceiros.
Criado em 2009, o Fundo Vale é o braço de fomento da mineradora para as agendas de natureza e clima. E o novo balanço registra uma mudança em sua função.
Nos 16 anos cobertos pelo reporte, o fundo aportou R$ 576 milhões em 169 projetos e 887 negócios. O que o documento sugere é que o valor desse braço deixa de estar no tamanho do cheque e passa a estar na engenharia financeira em torno dele.
O mecanismo por trás do multiplicador é familiar a quem trabalha com blended finance. Ao assumir as primeiras perdas de uma operação, dar garantias ou aceitar receber por último, o Fundo tira parte do risco da mesa e melhora a relação entre risco e retorno para os investidores que vêm depois.
É o tipo de reforço que soluções baseadas na natureza costumam não conseguir sozinhas, por operarem em cadeias pouco estruturadas, com ciclos longos e sem garantias ou histórico financeiro que um banco reconheça.
O próprio relatório, porém, evita tratar o 5,9 como regra. “A alavancagem não é automática. Ela varia conforme o mecanismo financeiro, a maturidade do negócio, os parceiros, o ambiente regulatório e o cenário macroeconômico”, pondera Grazielle Parenti, VP de Sustentabilidade da Vale.
++Leia mais: C&A soma R$ 45,7 milhões ao lucro com ESG e leva moda circular à Avenida Paulista
Pesa também o apoio não financeiro, de pesquisa a governança e mensuração.
O indicador mede a proporção entre o aporte do Fundo e os recursos que outros atores colocaram na mesma iniciativa, contabilizados só depois de validada a contribuição da organização para a entrada desse capital.
A tese que sustenta a virada é simples: a escala que as agendas de clima e natureza exigem não cabe no orçamento de nenhum financiador isolado, e só aparece quando recursos públicos, filantrópicos e privados se combinam. Daí a decisão de qualificar o capital filantrópico para induzir o mercado, em vez de bancar sozinho.
Na maior parte dos arranjos, o Fundo entra com recursos não reembolsáveis, via doações, apoio a estruturadores e desenho de teses de impacto. Em estruturas mais avançadas, como as ligadas à sua Meta Florestal 2030, a Vale também assume a posição de investidora.
Segundo a companhia, em cinco anos, foram mais de dez mecanismos estruturados ou apoiados, entre eles o Fundo VC Floresta e Clima, o Mecanismo Amazônia Viva, que opera o CRA Verde, e a frente de investimento da AMAZ.
O caso mais destacado é o da Belterra Agroflorestas, acompanhada pelo Fundo desde 2020 na estruturação financeira e na governança.
O trabalho de redução de risco ajudou a viabilizar o financiamento de sistemas agroflorestais e desembocou em uma rodada de equity de até R$ 75 milhões, em maio deste ano, o tipo de resultado usado para demonstrar que o modelo é bem sucedido.
“Além de aportar recursos, passamos a estruturar mecanismos financeiros inovadores, compartilhar riscos e atrair novos financiadores para agendas que ainda enfrentam barreiras de acesso a capital”, afirma Grazielle Parenti, VP de Sustentabilidade da Vale.
Por que uma mineradora constrói competência em finanças florestais? A resposta está na geografia do negócio: a principal operação da Vale fica na Amazônia, de onde sai cerca de 60% de sua produção, a mesma região onde a floresta em pé virou ativo estratégico.
Para uma companhia que carrega o passivo reputacional dos rompimentos de barragens em Mariana, em 2015, e Brumadinho, em 2019, a agenda de floresta e bioeconomia soma-se aos compromissos socioambientais e ao esforço de diversificar a economia dos territórios em que atua.
É nesse ponto que a agenda ambiental se aproxima de vez da financeira. O Fundo conduz a frente de recuperação de áreas da Meta Florestal 2030, compromisso voluntário de proteger e recuperar 500 mil hectares até o fim da década, além das obrigações legais.
Conforme o relatório, cerca de 45% já foi alcançado, aproximadamente 225 mil hectares. Nessa frente, foram R$ 292 milhões aportados diretamente nos negócios e outros R$ 38 milhões em suporte não financeiro, para mais de 25 mil hectares em modelos como regeneração natural assistida, sistemas agroflorestais e Integração Lavoura-Pecuária-Floresta.
A meta se encaixa ainda na estratégia climática global da companhia, que promete emissões líquidas zero nos Escopos 1 e 2 até 2050 e corte de 15% no Escopo 3 até 2035. Desde 2020, a Vale afirma ter destinado cerca de US$ 1,7 bilhão a mitigação e adaptação.
Recursos públicos e concessionais seguem indispensáveis nos estágios iniciais, justamente para reduzir risco e abrir caminho ao investidor privado que, sozinho, não entraria.
Ainda assim, há sinais de que essa dependência começa a diminuir. Parceiros corporativos, investidores de impacto e compradores de atributos ambientais já aparecem nas estruturas. E fundos especializados crescem, caso do Pátria Reforest Fund, que mira R$ 2 bilhões para restaurar áreas na Mata Atlântica.
Mas na bioeconomia amazônica os gargalos são também estruturais: risco alto, negócios pouco maduros, escala e governança frágeis, poucas garantias e ausência de infraestrutura, de laboratórios a plantas-piloto.
O Fundo então se coloca como uma espécie de infraestrutura financeira e institucional desse ecossistema, presente em iniciativas como o Mecanismo Financeiro Amazônia Viva, o Fundo Socioambiental Conexsus e o Sustenta.Bio, que cobre 15 áreas protegidas e 10 milhões de hectares na Amazônia.
Mas a escala da necessidade expõe o limite da filantropia: um estudo da International Chamber of Commerce estima que a bioeconomia do conhecimento movimenta US$ 2 bilhões por ano, pode chegar a US$ 140 bilhões até 2032 e exigirá US$ 15,7 bilhões em investimento na próxima década.
“Uma lacuna de US$ 15,7 bilhões não será superada apenas com doações. Será necessária a articulação entre capital público, filantrópico e privado, acompanhada de políticas públicas e do fortalecimento de todo o ecossistema”, afirma Parenti.
O primeiro ciclo da Teoria da Mudança 2020–2030 — o plano estratégico que o Fundo adotou para orientar e medir sua atuação na década — mostrou que a transformação nas agendas de floresta e clima não segue a lógica linear de metas com que costuma ser vendida.
Houve avanço na estruturação de negócios, na mobilização de capital e na articulação do setor. O crescimento e a autonomia financeira dos negócios apoiados, porém, vieram mais devagar do que o esperado, o que forçou o Fundo a buscar novas fontes de receita para sustentá-los, como os créditos de carbono.
“Aprendemos que os ciclos dos negócios socioambientais podem levar de cinco a dez anos para gerar retornos consistentes. Isso exige capital paciente, recursos flexíveis e soluções adaptadas às características de cada território”, diz Patricia Daros, Diretora de Natureza da Vale.
"Nossa atuação envolveu testar soluções, estruturar arranjos institucionais e financeiros ainda incipientes e fortalecer negócios e ecossistemas”, afirma a executiva.
Até 2030, segundo a organização, o sucesso deixará de ser medido só por hectares recuperados ou recursos mobilizados e passará a incluir resultados ambientais, econômicos e sistêmicos.
Ou seja, o teste real não será o tamanho do cheque que o Fundo assinou, e sim quantos dos negócios que ele destravou seguem captando quando o capital catalítico sai de cena.

title: Before-and-after images show effects of rain in drought-hit England and Wales
content:
The landscapes of southern England and Wales are slowly regaining their colour after this summer’s extreme heat.
The UK’s hottest summer on record left the south of the country dried out and brown, making the impact of the drought particularly visual.
As autumn begins, large parts of the UK are still officially in drought. And even if autumn is wetter than normal, some could still be in drought in the spring, according to the Environment Agency.
But some rain has returned, and with it the green, to the relief of many. Darren Share, the director of the royal parks, which manages Hyde Park and St James Park among others, recalls: “The grass was completely scorched off across all of our park network, it was quite shocking. The grass level had almost turned to dust.
“We’ve had heatwaves in the past but they’ve only been for short periods of time. The grass dies off, we get the rain again and then everything starts coming back quite quickly. This time it was just one [heatwave] after another.”
The extreme conditions not only changed the physical features of the parks, he said. “You could see that people were using the parks completely differently.”
Visitor numbers decreased significantly during the day and many sporting and volunteering activities were cancelled because of health and safety concerns.
The royal parks are not yet in full bloom again, but the difference between now and peak summer is stark. Share attributes the rapid regrowth to the resilience of grass. “I’m looking at the parks and seeing the grass come back to green. We’re very lucky that grass can tolerate that level of heat and will regenerate like we’re seeing now,” he said.
In Wales, which was hit by wildfires in mid-August, the death of grassy areas had a range of social and environmental effects. “I saw really thin cattle because they had no food for grazing,” said Carolyn Thomas, a climate activist and former Senedd member. “Farmers … had to go into their winter stock to keep their animals fed.
“Sheep and cows were hiding under the shade of trees barely moving. Some were lying down flat and I was thinking: ‘Are they dead?’”
The UK government has pledged £100m to “strengthen the country’s capacity to respond to extreme weather and wildfires”, but Thomas said she did not think this was the solution.
“If you have to evacuate your home because of a wildfire you can’t just think: ‘We need a bigger fire service and more helicopters that can drop water’,” she said. “We need prevention.”
Like southern England, the Welsh countryside is slowly returning to normal, much to Thomas’s pleasure. “Now I’m walking and seeing green fields,” she said. “It’s amazing. But we still have that loss as well and it’s going to take a while to recover.”
Groundwater and reservoir levels remain low and the government has urged water companies to continue their efficiency measures until normal levels are reached.

title: English vowel identification in noise shows reduced native-language influence: a behavioral study using machine-learning analysis of Chinese children
content: IntroductionNon-native listeners experience greater difficulty perceiving second-language (L2) speech in noise, yet whether first-language (L1) phonological skills continue to support L2 perception under adverse acoustic conditions remains unclear.MethodsWe examined English back-vowel identification in 52 Chinese fifth- (n = 25) and sixth-grade (n = 27) children under quiet, 5 dB SNR, and −5 dB SNR conditions. Chinese vowel identification in quiet was used to index L1 ability, and linear regression and random forest models were used to characterize associations among acoustic background, grade, and L1 perception.ResultsSixth graders outperformed fifth graders across conditions, but the grade advantage decreased as noise increased, with accuracy differences of 13.30%, 9.80%, and 3.20%, respectively. Chinese vowel identification significantly predicted English vowel identification in quiet but showed no significant predictive association under either noise condition. Random forest analyses complemented the specified linear model by revealing nonlinear predictive patterns, including a grade-by-noise interaction not detected by the linear model in this sample. These exploratory findings should be interpreted cautiously given the modest sample size (N= 52) and strict participant-level validation.DiscussionThe findings suggest that the association between quiet-measured L1 vowel identification and L2 vowel identification is context-dependent and attenuates under noisy listening conditions. They also indicate that grade-related advantages diminish as acoustic difficulty increases, while machine-learning analyses may provide complementary information about predictive patterns without establishing underlying cognitive mechanisms.

title: Nepal’s rhino census is getting a scientific makeover
content:
National
Nepal’s rhino census is getting a scientific makeover
Authorities are considering DNA sampling and camera traps to replace a decades-old method that relies on elephants and direct sightings.Manoj Paudel
Nepal is preparing to overhaul the way it counts its one-horned rhinos, moving away from a decades-old system that sends people into the jungle on elephants to spot and record the conserved animals.
The move comes as Nepal seeks better data on a rhino population that has recovered from historic lows but continues to face significant threats.
Nepal’s rhino population has risen sharply since it fell to about 100 in the 1960s, but 133 rhinos have died in and around Chitwan National Park over the past five years.
Authorities say the existing counting method is risky for survey teams and does not produce the kind of scientific data now needed to manage the population.
The Department of National Parks and Wildlife Conservation is considering genetic sampling, camera traps or a combination of the two for the next census. A committee will first prepare a protocol and conduct pilot studies before recommending a methodology.
“The department is preparing to revise the old method and adopt a new one,” said Haribhadra Acharya, a senior ecologist at the department. “We will conduct pilot studies to develop the methodology.”
Nepal currently has 752 one-horned rhinos, according to department data. More than 92 percent of them live in Chitwan National Park, making the park the centre of the country’s rhino conservation effort.
The 2021 census counted 694 rhinos in Chitwan, 38 in Bardiya National Park, 17 in Shuklaphanta National Park and three in Parsa National Park.
The next census is normally due after four or five years, but authorities are now preparing to change how it is conducted.
For decades, survey teams have divided rhino habitat into blocks and moved through them on elephants, spotting and counting the animals directly. Under the so-called ‘sweep operation’, elephants carrying the surveyors are positioned close enough for one team to see another as they search their assigned areas.
The method has become increasingly difficult to defend.
About 40 elephants were deployed each day during previous counts, with two counters riding on each elephant. The animals had to work from morning until evening and could become tired and aggressive.
There was also the danger of encounters with wild elephants.
During the 2021 census, a male wild elephant encountered one of the elephants being used by the survey team. The elephant carrying the counters bolted, throwing and dragging a technician who was injured. He remains disabled, Acharya said.
“Risk is high, and it is also difficult to obtain the actual data,” he said.
The department also says the equipment used in previous counts was inadequate and that the technology was not sufficiently scientific or reliable.
That is prompting officials to look beyond the traditional approach. Camera traps are already used to estimate tiger populations, while rhinos have generally been counted through direct observation.
“Tiger numbers are determined digitally through camera trapping, whereas rhinos have been counted by people seeing them directly,” Acharya said. “The tiger census is therefore considered scientific, while the rhino census has mainly been aimed at finding out the number of animals.”
A recovery with continuing threats
The proposed change in census methodology comes against the backdrop of a remarkable but uneven recovery.
Nepal had about 800 rhinos in the 1950s. By the following decade, their numbers had collapsed to around 100. Conservation programmes subsequently helped the population recover, turning the one-horned rhino into one of the country’s most recognisable wildlife species.
But the animals continue to die from a range of causes.
Chitwan recorded 22 rhino deaths in the fiscal year 2025–26, including 20 inside the national park and two in the surrounding national forest. The park recorded 30 deaths in 2024–25, 21 in 2023–24, 23 in 2022–23 and 37 in 2021–22.
Rhinos die naturally as they age, but deaths also result from fights between animals, getting trapped in marshes and mud, electrocution and, occasionally, tiger attacks. Poaching remains a conservation concern, although no rhino has been killed by poachers in Chitwan since October 2023, according to park officials.
“Conservation has not produced the results we had hoped for because of habitat-management problems and the limited resources available,” said Abinash Thapa Magar, information officer and conservation officer at Chitwan National Park.
Human-rhino conflict is another problem. Rhinos sometimes enter agricultural land and damage crops, increasing tensions between communities and wildlife.
Thapa Magar said awareness campaigns, greater vigilance and tighter security had helped reduce poaching.
“We do not have any concrete evidence yet about where the horns of poached rhinos end up or what they are used for,” he said.
The department has a 2024–34 action plan for rhino conservation.
More than a tourist attraction
For Nepal, the stakes go beyond the survival of a charismatic animal.
The greater one-horned rhino is found only in parts of Nepal and India. Its horn can grow to between 20 and 100 centimetres, while its massive body, thick folds of skin and distinctive appearance make it a major draw for wildlife tourists.
Hundreds of thousands of visitors come to Nepal each year, and rhino sightings are an important part of the country’s wildlife tourism industry.
“The rhino is a flagship species of riverine areas, so its ecological importance is equally significant,” said Dr Naresh Subedi, a former member-secretary of the National Trust for Nature Conservation.
Rhinos also alter the environment around them. By feeding on large grasses, they help keep forests and grasslands open and create habitat for smaller animals. For that reason, conservationists refer to them as ‘ecosystem engineers’.
Their relationship with other wildlife is also significant, according to Dr Ghana Shyam Gurung, a WWF Nepal representative.
“Saving rhinos also helps save tigers, and vice versa, so the species has a distinct importance,” Gurung said. “Rhinos are prehistoric animals, which is another reason people are fascinated by them.”
For tourists, the appeal is simpler. Nature guide Dinesh Giri said visitors often take elephant-back or jeep safaris to watch rhinos moving through their natural habitat, their massive bodies swaying as they walk or wallow in mud.
The animals are generally peaceful when left alone. But that can change quickly when they feel threatened. A frightened or angry rhino can run at high speed and attack.
Chitwan is the world’s second-largest habitat for the greater one-horned rhinoceros after Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve in Assam, India.

title: Government should have organised massive protest against insult to Mallikarjun Kharge, says Congress leader
content:
“The Congress government in Karnataka should have organised a massive protest against the insult suffered by Mallikarjun Kharge, AICC chairman, after the ‘purification ritual’ incident in Haldwani. I am disappointed that the Congress did not protest properly,’’ Prasad Abbayya, MLA and Congress leader, said in Davangere on Sunday.
“Due to his pro-public efforts and integrity, Mallikarjun Kharge has evolved into a mass leader with a clean image. He has grown beyond any caste affiliation. It is a matter of disgrace that he was insulted by the right-wing forces who performed purification after his visit to Haldwani. In fact, this was such a grave offence against the constitutional principle of equality that it is an insult to all Indian citizens. We need to realise this and oppose such attempts strongly,’’ Mr. Abbayya, the Dalit leader from Hubballi, said.
He was speaking at an event to felicitate meritorious students organised by the Chalavadi community in Davanagere. He urged community members to stand united with Home Minister Priyank Kharge. “The Home Minister is forging ahead due to his knowledge and clarity of thought, but he is facing verbal attacks from vested interests. We must stand firmly behind him,” he said.
“Ideology is more important for me than power. I once said that compared to ideology, power is like the chappals I wear. I stand by it even now,’’ H.C. Mahadevappa, former Minister, said.
“When Janata Dal (Secular) leaders expelled former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, we all quit. Some of his followers organised an AHINDA rally in Hubballi. I was going there when H.D. Deve Gowda sent word with someone saying I should come back to the JD(S). The messenger told me that I would be made a Minister if I came back to the party. It was then that I said that power meant nothing to me in front of ideology,’’ Dr. Mahadevappa said.
“We must remain committed to our ideology. It was B.R. Ambedkar who gave us democracy. The British government was delaying the transfer of power to Indians. It was Dr. Ambedkar who persuaded the then British Prime Minister Winston Churchill to allow the transfer of power. We should all be proud of this fact. It is our responsibility to make this democracy work. All the deprived communities, the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, various other backward classes, minorities, and others must remain united,” he said.
Minister K.S. Basavantappa alleged that outsourcing agencies were fleecing pourakarmikas in some places. “I am the son of pourakarmikas. I will not allow this. We will bring in strict measures to stop it,’’ he said. The Minister added that he would request Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to institute an award for pourakarmikas in the name of former Minister B. Basavalingappa. “Mr. Basavalingappa was a great leader who banned the practice of manual scavenging in the State. It is because of him that civic workers today lead dignified lives, he said.
“Mr. Basavantappa urged the various factions of Dalit associations to unite. We should become true Ambedkarites and internalise his ideology. We should not go around forming associations for the sake of forming them,’’ he said.
Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara inaugurated the event at the S.S. Mallikarjun Cultural Centre. Sri Jnana Prakasha Swamiji, former Minister H.C. Mahadevappa, Minister K.S. Basavantappa, Prabha Mallikarjun, MP, Samarth Shamanur, MLA, and other community leaders were present.

title: Američka tvrtka zakinula dostavljače za plaće, mora platiti milijune. "Zeznuli smo"
content:
Američka tvrtka zakinula dostavljače za plaće, mora platiti milijune. "Zeznuli smo"
AMERIČKA tvrtka za dostavu hrane DoorDash morat će platiti 131,5 milijuna dolara, odnosno oko 115 milijuna eura, u sklopu nagodbe zbog optužbi da je svojim dostavljačima u New Yorku isplaćivala preniske plaće. Vijest je danas objavio gradonačelnik New Yorka Zohran Mamdani. Gradske vlasti opisale su dogovor kao najveću nagodbu s radnicima u povijesti grada.
Nagodba obvezuje tvrtku i na uvođenje novog sustava nadzora, čiji je cilj osigurati da DoorDash ubuduće poštuje gradske propise o plaćama dostavljača. U službenom priopćenju DoorDash je priznao pogreške. "Jednostavno rečeno, zeznuli smo", stoji u izjavi.
"Iako te pogreške nisu bile namjerne, to ih ne opravdava. U DoorDashu se ponosimo operativnom izvrsnošću, a ovo nije bilo ni izvrsno ni prihvatljivo. Dostavljači moraju biti plaćeni u cijelosti i na vrijeme, svaki put. Žao nam je što smo iznevjerili naše dostavljače", poručili su iz tvrtke.
Veći dio iznosa iz nagodbe bit će isplaćen za više od 260.000 radnika kojima je DoorDash isplaćivao manje iznose, kasnio s isplatama ili im uopće nije platio za obavljene dostave, potvrdili su iz gradske uprave. Tvrtka će gradu platiti i oko 16 milijuna dolara na ime građanskih kazni i ostalih troškova.
Mamdani: Vraćamo novac koji su radnici zaradili
"Kada radnik zaradi plaću, zaslužuje da mu se ona i isplati. Ne sutra, ne nakon tužbe, nego na vrijeme i u punom iznosu", izjavio je Mamdani. "DoorDash je zakinuo više od 260.000 radnika, a danas im taj novac vraćamo", najavio je.
Iz DoorDasha su objasnili da su mnoge pogreške pri plaćanju bile uzrokovane "tehničkim greškama ili su se dogodile u kompliciranim situacijama". Pritom se misli na dostave izvan gradskih granica, narudžbe s više mjesta preuzimanja ili isporuke te na otkazane ili djelomično obavljene narudžbe.
Ovo nije prvi put da se tvrtka nagodila s vlastima. Prošle je godine pristala platiti gotovo 17 milijuna dolara zbog optužbi da je napojnice kupaca koristila za subvencioniranje plaća dostavljača. Umjesto da novac od napojnica dobiju kao dodatak na zajamčenu zaradu, tvrtka im je time pokrivala dio osnovne plaće.

title: How Restoring Nature Helped Shape Three Future Conservationists
content:
A morning spent planting wildflowers or clearing invasive species may seem ordinary, but for some young volunteers, those first moments caring for nature become the start of something much bigger.
Environmental restoration is often measured by visible outcomes—healthier creeks, thriving native plants, returning wildlife, and restored habitats. Those achievements matter, but another lasting impact is harder to measure. Every restoration project can also shape the people who take part, inspiring future scientists, conservationists, and environmental leaders.
That philosophy is reflected in the work of Grassroots Ecology, a California nonprofit that restores local ecosystems while engaging community members as active participants. Rather than simply teaching people about conservation, the organization encourages volunteers to experience it firsthand. Whether they’re planting native habitat, restoring creek corridors, or monitoring wildlife, participants discover that caring for nature is something they can do—not just something they can admire from a distance.
For some, those experiences leave a lasting impression.
When Meili first joined Grassroots Ecology, she was looking for an opportunity to spend more time outdoors while contributing to habitat restoration. What she found was something far more meaningful. Working directly with native landscapes sparked a fascination with the hidden relationships that allow ecosystems to thrive.
Instead of seeing forests as collections of individual trees, she began to appreciate the intricate web of life beneath the surface. Questions that emerged during restoration work gradually grew into a passion for ecological research.
Today, Meili is working as a Research Technician at Stanford University and will begin pursuing her PhD there in mid-September 2026, studying mycorrhizal fungi—the underground networks that help trees exchange nutrients, communicate, and become more resilient to environmental stress. Although her research now takes her into laboratories and forests, she traces much of her enthusiasm for ecology back to those early restoration experiences that transformed environmental science from an abstract subject into something living, dynamic, and deeply interconnected.
Rohan’s journey followed a different path but began in much the same way.
As a participant in Grassroots Ecology’s restoration efforts, he discovered that conservation wasn’t limited to forests, parks, or open spaces close to home. Caring for local habitats introduced him to the broader world of environmental science and the many ways people can help protect the planet.
That growing curiosity eventually led him to internships with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), where he gained experience in marine research and ocean mapping. Today, he continues his studies in ocean science, building the technical knowledge needed to better understand and protect marine ecosystems.
Although his work now focuses on the ocean, his story illustrates an important truth: a single opportunity to care for one local environment can inspire a lifelong commitment to protecting many others.
For Meera, the greatest lesson wasn’t only about restoring habitats—it was about the values that restoration requires.
Working alongside experienced staff and fellow volunteers showed her that healthy ecosystems are built gradually through patience, collaboration, and consistent care. Native plants don’t flourish overnight, and meaningful restoration depends on people willing to invest in landscapes for years, not days.
Those lessons stayed with her long after her time as a volunteer with Grassroots Ecology ended. Today, Meera leads restoration projects at the University of California, Davis, while continuing to support habitat restoration efforts with Santa Clara County Parks. In late September 2026, she will return to Grassroots Ecology as an AmeriCorps fellow, bringing her experience back to the organization where her connection to restoration first began. Her journey reflects how early experiences in conservation can continue to shape a person’s work—and bring them back to the places where it all started.
Although Meili, Rohan, and Meera chose different careers—forest ecology, ocean science, and habitat restoration—they all share something in common. Their journeys began not in classrooms or laboratories, but outdoors, working alongside others to restore the landscapes around them.
Their stories remind us that environmental stewardship can begin with surprisingly ordinary experiences. A volunteer event, a few hours spent planting native species, or the chance to ask questions while working alongside knowledgeable mentors can change how someone sees both nature and their own ability to make a difference.
As communities around the world invest in restoring ecosystems, they are also investing in something less visible but equally important: the people who will care for those places in the future. Healthy habitats need dedicated stewards just as much as they need native plants and clean water.
The native species planted today will continue growing for years to come. So will the curiosity, confidence, and sense of purpose that restoration inspires in the people who help put them in the ground. In that way, every restoration project nurtures two futures at once—one rooted in healthier ecosystems, and another in the next generation of environmental leaders who will continue protecting them.

title: Journée de la paix au Niger : Niamey mobilise sa jeunesse au stade Kountché
content: © Haute Autorité à la Consolidation de la Paix NIAMEY, 21 septembre 2026 — Face aux multiples défis sécuritaires et économiques qui traversent la région, la capitale nigérienne a choisi la voie du rassemblement populaire. En effet, ce lundi, les travées et l'esplanade du Stade Général Seyni Kountché ont servi de cadre au coup d'envoi d'une semaine d'engagement citoyen marquant la Journée internationale de la paix. Sous le slogan « Investir dans la paix, pour tous, partout, chaque jour », la Haute Autorité à la Consolidation de la Paix et les agences des Nations Unies pilotent conjointement cette initiative, avec l’appui de structures institutionnelles locales telles que le Fonds de Solidarité pour la Sauvegarde de la Patrie (FSSP). Une mobilisation inclusive par l'effort physique au stade Seyni Kountché Pour amorcer cette série de rencontres, les organisateurs ont privilégié l'action sportive et inclusive dès les premières heures de la journée. Un cross de masse a réuni des centaines de participants sur des parcours adaptés de 4 et 8 kilomètres, tandis qu'une épreuve dédiée en tricycles a mis à l'honneur des personnes en situation de handicap. En fait, cette approche opérationnelle a transformé une célébration protocolaire en un événement communautaire vivant, capable de rapprocher des populations issues d'horizons divers. Le Conseil National de la Jeunesse honoré du Prix national de la Paix Par ailleurs, le volet institutionnel de la journée a été marqué par une distinction majeure : l'attribution du Prix national de la Paix au Conseil national de la jeunesse du Niger (CNJN) par le Ministre de la jeunesse des sports et de la culture, Sidi Mohamed Almahmoud. Cette récompense vient saluer la contribution proactive des organisations de jeunesse au maintien du dialogue social et à la prévention des tensions intercommunautaires. Parallèlement aux cérémonies d'ouverture et à l'exposition des partenaires techniques, un panel d'experts et de dirigeants a ouvert les débats sur les voies et moyens de pérenniser la stabilité dans les zones vulnérables. Sept jours d'actions citoyennes pour ancrer une culture de stabilité La programmation ne se limite pas aux événements du 21 septembre. Les acteurs publics, les diplomates et la société civile prévoient une suite de débats thématiques, d'ateliers interactifs et de campagnes de terrain tout au long de la semaine. Ainsi, l'objectif affiché par les autorités administratives est de dépasser la commémoration symbolique pour doter les communautés de leviers durables favorisant la tolérance, le dialogue intergénérationnel et le développement humain. En somme, la célébration de la Journée internationale de la paix se poursuit jusqu’au 25 septembre à Niamey. La réussite de cette semaine d'engagement se mesurera à sa capacité à transformer l'élan collectif en actions concrètes au quotidien. En impliquant directement la jeunesse ainsi que les communautés vulnérables dès les premières étapes, Niamey entend poser les bases d'une cohésion sociale durable, capable de résister aux tensions régionales et d'inspirer de nouvelles dynamiques de développement sur l'ensemble du territoire.
